```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

This workflow uses invented inpatient discharges from `nis_example()`. In a
study, use the path to your converted annual Parquet files and supply your
own diagnosis definitions and eligibility rules.

## Open, project, and flag

Choose the study years in `nis_open()`. Select the columns needed for the
analysis, keeping the design fields and the diagnosis slots used by the flag.
The query stays in DuckDB. The diagnosis flag checks every slot by default.

```{r cohort}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  dplyr::select(nis_vars_design(), nis_vars_dx(), AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  dplyr::mutate(adult = AGE >= 18, death = as.integer(DIED))

nis_attrition(nis, adult = adult, heart_failure = heart_failure, by_year = TRUE)
```

`nis_vars_design()` keeps `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS`, `NIS_STRATUM`, `DISCWT` and,
when present, `DQTR`. If a prior selection removed one of the four required
fields, `nis_design()` reports the missing field. See
[Defining cohorts](cohorts.html) for principal diagnoses, exclusions, procedure
flags, and code-system choices.

## Estimate within the adult domain

Pass the eligibility flag to `cohort` so the variance calculation can account
for sampled hospital-years with no eligible discharges. `keep` limits what the
design brings into R, and the design labels retained HCUP fields. The flag
groups compare adult discharges with and without a matching diagnosis.

```{r design}
design <- nis |>
  nis_design(cohort = adult, keep = c(heart_failure, AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED, death))

estimates <- design |>
  dplyr::group_by(heart_failure) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
    mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

This estimates totals across both study years. Use `annualize = TRUE` for
average annual totals when each included year represents a whole year.
For annual estimates, keep the original weights and group by `YEAR`. See
[Survey design and weighting](survey-design.html) for pooling and coverage.

## Make a table and fit a model

Use the same design for the descriptive table and regression. The model
adjusts for age, sex, and year in this invented example. Review the model
sample and missingness when reporting a real analysis.

```{r table-one, eval=rlang::is_installed(c("gtsummary", "cardx", "gt"))}
table_one <- design |>
  gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(by = heart_failure, include = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED))
nis_suppress(table_one)
```

```{r model}
fit <- survey::svyglm(
  death ~ heart_failure + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)
```

## Review disclosure before exporting

The table above masks statistics using corresponding unweighted counts and
hospital support. For a data-frame summary, attach those counts explicitly.
This fixture has recorded LOS for every discharge. With missing LOS, use
counts for the records contributing to that mean.

```{r disclosure}
reviewed <- estimates |>
  dplyr::left_join(nis_cell_counts(design, by = "heart_failure"), by = "heart_failure") |>
  nis_suppress(
    count_col = "n",
    hospital_col = "hospitals",
    weighted_cols = c("discharges", "discharges_se", "mean_los", "mean_los_se")
  )
reviewed
```

Review disclosure across tables, models, and related totals before sharing.
Keep work in a private directory. See [Disclosure and suppression](disclosure.html).

```{r export, eval=FALSE}
utils::write.csv(reviewed, "discharges-reviewed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Project before collecting

When a step needs a data frame, put `select()` before `collect()` so DuckDB
can read the requested columns from Parquet. In a Windows benchmark, fresh R
4.6.1 processes with DuckDB 1.5.2 selected the same seven columns from
480,000 invented rows and 188 source columns. Peak process commit was
206 MiB with projection before collection and 1,379 MiB with projection
after collection. The difference measures one synthetic workload. Peak
memory depends on the data, query, and system.

To reproduce the measurement from the easyNIS source directory on Windows,
install the package and run these commands with a new scratch directory.

```sh
Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R prepare local/loop/wide-invented
Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R early local/loop/wide-invented
Rscript --vanilla tools/benchmark-column-projection.R late local/loop/wide-invented
```
